standard_prerequisites.name: The reduction of constructibility to retrocompact opens, cited from the topology chapter: it suffices to show that inverse images of retrocompact opens are retrocompact
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the constructible case to a statement about retrocompact opens.

standard_prerequisites.name: An open immersion with retrocompact source is quasi-compact, and quasi-compactness survives base change, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the base change of the retrocompact open is quasi-compact, which is exactly retrocompactness in the source.

standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of locally constructible subsets by their traces on affine opens, cited from the properties chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the locally constructible case to the constructible case on an affine chart.

core_obligations: Constructible case, reduction: to show that inverse images of constructible sets are constructible it is enough to treat retrocompact opens, because constructible sets are finite combinations of such opens (proof lines 4564-4567).

Constructible case, conclusion: the significance of a retrocompact open is that its inclusion is quasi-compact, so its base change along any morphism is quasi-compact, hence its inverse image is retrocompact in the source, which gives constructibility of the inverse image (proof lines 4567-4572).

Locally constructible case: at a point choose affine neighbourhoods V of the image and U of the point with the image of U inside V, so that the trace of the subset on V is constructible by the cited characterization, apply the constructible case to the restriction of the morphism, and translate back through the identity between the traces (proof lines 4573-4583).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to retrocompact opens and use quasi-compactness of base change (proof lines 4564-4572).
For the local version, restrict to affine charts and apply the global case there (proof lines 4573-4583).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the inverse image of a (locally) constructible subset under an arbitrary morphism of schemes is again (locally) constructible (statement lines 4556-4562). The counted proof separates the two notions: for constructible subsets it reduces to retrocompact opens and uses that retrocompactness of an open immersion is quasi-compactness, which survives base change, and for locally constructible subsets it restricts to a pair of affine charts and applies the global case (proof lines 4564-4583). It is H2: the argument is complete in the counted span and the inputs are standard topological and scheme-theoretic criteria.
